terms.meaning: The committee of villagers in every Chola village.
The elected village committee of each kurram, also called perumguri; its members were perumakkal.
The Hoysala king's special guards, who gave up their lives when he died.
A carved female figure on the pillar brackets, as at the Chennakeshava temple, Beluru.
The faith Ramanujacharya spread across Karnataka under Vishnuvardhana.

items.name: Founders of the Chola kingdom
items.formula: Karikala Chola, by Sangam literature; Vijayalaya Chola revived it with Thanjavur as capital.
items.example: They ruled from the 9th to the 13th century, after the Pallavas.

items.name: Rajaraja Chola I
items.formula: Beat the Cheras, Gangas and Pandyas, built a navy and captured Sri Lanka.
items.example: He built the Brihadeeshwara temple at Thanjavur.

items.name: Chola village self-government
items.formula: Members were elected, but only Sanskrit scholars and rich people could stand.
items.example: One-sixth of the crop was taken as tax.

items.name: Chola irrigation
items.formula: They built many lakes, including Bellandur lake near Bangalore.
items.example: A huge pond at Gangaikonda Cholapuram.

items.name: Brihadeeshwara temple
items.formula: 500 feet tall in a courtyard 250 feet wide, with a 200 foot shikara.

items.name: Chola temples in Karnataka
items.formula: Aprameya near Channapatna, Choleshwara at Begur, Mukteshwara near Binnamangala.

items.name: Tamil literature under the Cholas
items.formula: Kamba's Ramayana, Sekkilar's Periya Purana, Thirukkadeva's Jeevaka Chintamani.
items.example: The empire weakened under Rajendra Chola III and fell to the Pandyas.

items.name: How the Hoysalas got their name
items.formula: Sala killed a tiger at Sosevuru (Angadi, Mudigere taluk) when the monk Sudatta said "Hoysala!".

items.name: Vishnuvardhana
items.formula: Won Gangavadi from the Cholas, title Talakadugonda; built the Kirtinarayan temple and Chennakeshava at Belur.
items.example: Vikramaditya VI of the Chalukyas defeated him.

items.name: Hoysala administration
items.formula: Provincial system; gowda, senabova and talawara in villages.
items.example: Lakes: Shanti Sagara, Ballalaraya Samudra, Vishnu Samudra. The kingdom declined under Ballala III.

items.name: Hoysala literature
items.formula: Janna: Yashodhara Charite. Harihara: Girija Kalyana. Raghavanka: Harishchandra Kavya. Keshiraja: Shabdamani Darpana.

items.name: Features of Hoysala temples
items.formula: Carved in soap stone, with a star-shaped sanctum, jagati, decorative panels, shikara and pillars.

items.name: Hoysala temples and sculptors
items.formula: Halebidu's Hoysaleshwara (built by Ketamalla); Somanathapura's Keshava (by Somadandanayaka).
items.example: Sculptors: Dasoja, Chavana, Jakana and Dankana.

mistakes.text: Brihadeeshwara at Thanjavur is Chola; Chennakeshava at Belur is Hoysala.
Talakadugonda was Vishnuvardhana's title for taking Gangavadi from the Cholas; Vatapikonda was a Pallava title.
Chola village elections were not open to all: only Sanskrit scholars and the rich could stand.
